ML Ratchet · Wildfire · Phase 2

FireCast

Where will a wildfire be tomorrow afternoon? A small network learned it from simulated fires only, then sat one exam on real ones.

Input: today's mapped burn scar, the active fire line, VIIRS satellite hot spots and the gridMET weather for today and tomorrow. Output: the chance that each 90 m cell has burned by the next afternoon satellite pass.

Explorer

Twelve exam fire-days drawn at random with a fixed seed, four each from small (under 5 km²), medium (5–50 km²) and large fires. None were picked by hand. Each map is the 10 km scoring window around the fire, at 90 m.

Weather lab

Change tomorrow's weather for the selected fire-day and run the network again. The page runs the same 374k-weight U-Net as the Python release (JavaScript and numpy agree to 2×10⁻⁶ in the logits). It takes a few seconds. The lab runs on the map window with 8-bit inputs, so its map differs from the Python forecast by 0.002–0.008 in probability on average.

The exam

Means over growth fire-days (days with any new burn), with 95 % bootstrap intervals that resample whole fires. Scored cells: unburned cells within 10 km of the burned area at issue time (firedata's score window). Baselines are B's, from FireData, on exactly the same fire-days.

Are the probabilities honest?

Pooled exam cells, grouped by forecast probability. On the diagonal, a 30 % forecast burns 30 % of the time.

AP on growth days, by burned area at issue time.

Against the physics simulator itself

Every rung, kept or not

The ratchet

A new model replaces the old one only if it scores more than 0.01 AP better on a frozen set of simulated fires and loses no more than 5 % AP on the 40 real dev fires (535 fire-days). The frozen set is rebuilt whenever the simulator's physics change, and every rung is re-scored on it.

Recipe

How it was built

1 · BurnFireSim spreads fires for 2–8 days on real LANDFIRE fuels and real HRRR weather from dev and non-exam places, with random fuel moisture, spread-rate error, wind error, night slow-down, spotting and growing containment.
2 · ObserveFireSim's satellite emulator turns each fire into S-NPP VIIRS hot spots at real overpass times, with cloud gaps. A dev-fitted emulator turns those into FEDS-style perimeters and fire lines.
3 · LearnA U-Net with 374k weights reads 22 map layers and 22 weather and fire numbers, and predicts next-day burn probability. 1,083 simulated fires, 4,402 fire-days.
4 · CheckTwin tests replay each real dev fire-day in the simulator and compare. Probabilities are calibrated on dev only: two numbers and a threshold.

Twin test: simulated vs real growth

Median log₁₀ of simulated over real new burned area on the same dev fire-days, by the fire's age. Zero means the simulator grows fires as fast as reality.

Limits

    Release

    Use it

    firecast-v1.0.zip holds a numpy + scipy model (no torch), the weights, a demo on three real exam fire-days that runs in seconds, the model card and every training script.

    import firecast as fc
net  = fc.FireCastNP('firecast_weights.npz')
prob = fc.predict(net, day)        # day: burned mask, fire line, VIIRS pixels, gridMET (see README)
yes  = prob >= net.thr             # dev-fitted threshold

    Data. MTBS perimeters (USGS/USFS), FEDS fire atlas (Chen et al. 2022), VIIRS active fire (NASA FIRMS / LANCE), gridMET (Abatzoglou 2013), LANDFIRE (USGS/USFS), HRRR (NOAA, AWS open data), splits and baselines from FireData. Physics: FireSim (Rothermel 1972, Albini 1976, Anderson 1983, Van Wagner 1977, Nelson 2000). Part of ML Ratchet: trained on physics, graded on reality.
